payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Florencio, Robena, Salvador, Wenona

payload.content: Hello team, I am Robena. I see we have several tasks related to data-science and mobile-development. I am skilled in data-science and have availability for 4 hours. I notice the low-priority data-science tasks have relatively low costs for me, and the high-priority mobile-development tasks have very high costs for me. I am considering taking one of the data-science tasks with lower cost to optimize our team's overall efficiency. What are others planning to take?

Hello Robena and team, this is Florencio. I have strong skills in data-science and 4 hours availability. I see you prefer data-science tasks with lower costs. I can consider taking one of the data-science tasks as well, but I am also willing to take on mobile-development tasks if someone else prefers the data-science ones. Let's try to cover more tasks efficiently without overlapping choices.

Hello team, Wenona here. I have strong data-science skills and 6 hours available. I see that the data-science tasks are low priority but manageable in cost for me, while the mobile-development tasks have very high costs for me due to effort and skills mismatch. I am inclined to pick one of the data-science tasks to help complete more tasks efficiently. What are others leaning towards?

Hello all, I am Wenona. I am focusing on data-science tasks given my skill fit and reasonable costs. I encourage others with better mobile-development skills to pick those high-priority tasks for better overall score. Let's coordinate to avoid overlap and maximize coverage.

Hello team, Salvador here. I have moderate skills in data-science and frontend with 5 hours availability. I see others lean towards data-science tasks for coverage and efficiency. I could also consider low-cost data-science tasks to help complete more tasks without overlap. Any preferences or plans from Robena, Florencio, or Wenona regarding specific data-science subtasks (implement, review, test, docs, triage)?

I suggest Wenona or Florencio consider taking 'implement' or 'test' for ISSUE-0001 as these require more effort, while I am open to taking 'review', 'docs', or 'triage' which have lower effort and cost for me. This way, we can efficiently split the data-science tasks among us without duplications.

Hello team, I appreciate the coordination so far. Given my 4 hours availability and strong fit in data-science, I am considering taking the 'implement' task for ISSUE-0001 as it matches my skills and fits my time well. I see Florencio and Wenona are likely to cover other data-science tasks, so I propose Florencio or Wenona take 'test' or 'review', and Salvador can pick 'docs' or 'triage' as suggested. This way, we maximize task coverage without overlap. Thoughts?

To the whole team, I am confirming my preference for ISSUE-0001::implement in data-science. Please notify if you'd prefer to take this or if you have other suggestions to optimize coverage and cost. Let's finalize soon to maximize our sprint outcome.

Hello team, this is Florencio. I see Robena prefers to take 'implement' for ISSUE-0001 in data-science, which fits well. I am willing to take 'test' for ISSUE-0001 in data-science as it matches my skills and availability. Wenona or Salvador could consider 'review', 'docs', or 'triage' to cover all data-science subtasks efficiently. Wenona, Salvador, please consider picking 'review', 'docs', or 'triage' for ISSUE-0001 data-science to complement Robena's 'implement' and my 'test' choices. This will ensure complete coverage of the data-science tasks with minimal overlap and better team efficiency. Let me know your preferences so we can finalize our assignments.

Hello Florencio and Salvador, I am considering taking the 'review' task for ISSUE-0001 in data-science. This fits my skills and availability well. Please let me know if this works for you so we can avoid overlap and maximize our coverage.

I see Robena plans to take 'implement' and Florencio plans to take 'test' for ISSUE-0001. Salvador, are you leaning towards 'docs' or 'triage'? I want to coordinate to ensure no duplicated picks and full coverage for ISSUE-0001 data-science tasks.

Reminder to team: Robena confirmed 'implement', Florencio 'test', Wenona 'review' for ISSUE-0001. Salvador, please confirm if you take 'docs' or 'triage' to complete the data-science tasks efficiently without overlap.
